limits Every limit below is copied from the manufacturer's manual or spec page, with the link, and the date we read it. Models we could not source are left out. Model Air fry max Preheat Source Ninja Air Fryer AF101 Basket · — 400°F / 205°C Manual Manual 2026-10-28 Ninja Air Fryer Pro AF141 Basket · — 400°F / 205°C Manual Manual 2026-10-28 Ninja Air Fryer Max XL AF161 Basket · — 400°F / 205°C Max Crisp to 450°F Manual Manual 2026-10-28 Ninja DoubleStack XL SL401 Dual-zone · 10 qt / 9.5 L 450°F / 230°C Default setting, max not stated Not stated Manual 2026-10-28 Ninja Foodi Digital Air Fry Oven SP101 Toaster-oven combo · — 450°F / 230°C Built-in step Manual 2026-10-28 Max temperature of every sourced model → When Max Crisp is the right button Take oven fries baked at 450°F for 20 minutes. On the Max XL's Air Fry they convert to 400°F for 16 minutes, checked from minute 11. The oven temperature is above what Air Fry reaches, so the converter holds at the limit and gives the time back. Shake the basket around minute 8. Max Crisp is right when the bag of frozen food says to air fry it, or when Ninja's own chart lists Max Crisp. It suits food that is already cooked and only needs a hard, fast finish. It is wrong for raw chicken, a tray bake or anything that has to cook through: you cannot turn it down, and the outside races ahead of the middle. The button name is not the number The Air Fryer Pro has a Max Crisp button too, but its guide puts every function, Max Crisp included, at 400°F. The name tells you what the button is for, not how hot it gets, so our table lists what each owner's guide states. The DoubleStack XL and the Foodi Digital Air Fry Oven are different again: Air Fry itself goes to 450°F, so a hot oven recipe converts without being held back. The oven counts as oven-style, with racks and a larger cavity, and gets the gentler oven-style conversion. Preheating a Ninja The basket models do not preheat on their own. Their guides recommend 3 minutes: choose the function and temperature, run it empty, then add the food. The converted times assume a hot basket. The DoubleStack XL's guide says it needs no preheat, and the Foodi oven preheats by itself, showing PRE until it is ready. Related Frozen fries 400°F · 15 min · shake ×2 Chicken wings 400°F · 22 min · flip at 11 Homemade fries 380°F · 18 min · shake ×2 Oven to air fryer converter → Cosori air fryer conversion → Philips Airfryer conversion → Instant Vortex air fryer conversion → Frequently asked questions What is the maximum temperature on a Ninja air fryer? Air Fry stops at 400°F on the Ninja basket models we have sourced. Max Crisp on the Max XL runs at 450°F, and the DoubleStack XL and Foodi oven air fry up to 450°F. The table links each model's guide. Can I set Max Crisp to a lower temperature? No. The Max XL guide says the temperature cannot be adjusted in Max Crisp. If you need less heat, use Air Fry and set it yourself. Should I use Max Crisp for oven recipes? Usually not. Convert the recipe for Air Fry instead. Max Crisp is meant for frozen, pre-cooked food that only needs crisping. Do I need to preheat my Ninja? On the basket models, yes: the guides recommend 3 minutes. The DoubleStack XL manual does not mention it, and the Foodi oven preheats on its own. Why are the Foodi 2-Basket models not in the table? We read the DZ201, DZ401 and DZ550 owner's guides in full. They give chart settings and probe targets, never an Air Fry maximum, so we left them out.
